Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sarah — appreciated the thoughtful questions from the ML and product teams. Quick recap and the shortlist we discussed for the POC.

Key outcomes from the demo:
- ACME is focused on customer-facing summarization (500-2k token documents) and an internal classification pipeline for sensitive ticket routing.
- Primary constraints: tight 200ms token latency SLA for realtime snippets, and strict PII handling (want private deployment option later).
- Success metrics: mean ROUGE/F1 on our eval set, <25ms per-token inference on dedicated infra for short prompts, and cost target ~x0.2 of current vendor spend.

Recommended model shortlist (first pass):
1) Llama3-70B (int8, sharded) — highest quality on long-context summarization; estimated 35–50ms/token on our Dedicated config for batched requests, best for fidelity but higher infra cost.
2) RedStone-13B (4-bit quant) — balanced: good summarization and classification, ~12–18ms/token, much lower cost than 70B, good candidate for initial POC.
3) Mistral-Instruct-7B — low-cost, low-latency option for classification and short-summary fallbacks; quality lower on long docs but strong for tickets and quick responses.

Attached: eval_report_ACME_v1.pdf (benchmarks on your sample data), prompt_set_ACME_v1.json (initial prompt templates + eval prompts). Also linking the benchmark page and our HubSpot deal for tracking.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick internal review from your infra/security (send over any additional security questionnaire).
- Confirm which model(s) you want in the 2-week POC (recommended: RedStone-13B + Mistral-7B to validate quality vs cost).
- Schedule POC kickoff: can do Wed/Thu next week.

Let me know availability — happy to jump on a 30-min follow to walk through the eval report.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Sarah — Dylan from Redwood infra/solutions. Answering your three bullets with concrete numbers from the ACME eval run (see attached PDF and the benchmark link):

1) Latency (samples from eval set, p50 / p95 per-token on our Dedicated profile):
- Llama3-70B (int8 sharded): p50 ~28ms/token, p95 ~65ms/token (long-context performance; p95 increases with >2k context)
- RedStone-13B (4-bit): p50 ~14ms/token, p95 ~28ms/token (stable for your 500–2k docs with batching)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: p50 ~6–9ms/token, p95 ~13–18ms/token (best tail behavior)

Note: those per-token numbers translate to end-to-end generation time dependent on output length and batching. For short interactive snippets (<=200 tokens), RedStone-13B end-to-end p95 was ~220–260ms in our setup with default batching; tuning batch size and using prefix KV caching can drop that below 200ms.

2) Cost (rough steady-state monthly estimate for 1M tokens/day; includes reserved infra amortized + token compute):
- Llama3-70B (int8): ~$40k–$55k/month (highest quality, highest infra spend)
- RedStone-13B (4-bit): ~$9k–$14k/month (best cost/quality tradeoff for POC)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: ~$3k–$5k/month (low-cost fallback for classification and lightweight summarization)

These are ballparks; we can provide a detailed pricing sheet if you confirm POC targets. Pricing assumes Redwood Dedicated reserved nodes. Hosted API pricing differs but is typically ~20–30% higher for same SLAs.

Quality/regression notes:
- We ran the ACME eval suite (included prompts) across the models. Llama3-70B gives the best ROUGE/F1 for long-doc summarization; RedStone-13B is within ~6–9% of 70B on average but with significantly lower cost and much better latency.
- We recommend adding a small continuous-eval job to catch quality regressions (daily run against the prompt set; we can host the eval harness). This is especially important if you use quantized variants in production — we track drift/regression with alerting.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm POC model(s): RedStone-13B + Mistral-7B (recommended) or Llama3-70B if fidelity is prioritized.
- Sign the POC SOW (I’ll have a draft to procurement within 24h).
- Kicking off infra onboarding + security review in parallel.

Links: benchmark summary: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2027-model-benchmarks
HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-042

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
